title: Shall Men Pretend to Pleasure
description: Shall Men Pretend to Pleasure in Tonic Solfa to GREENLAND, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 3, “We were once as you are”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens and Sixes Double (7.6.7.6.7.6.7.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to GREENLAND; any other Sevens and Sixes Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Shall men pre-tend to plea-sure Who nev-er knew the Lord? Can all the world-ling's trea-sure True peace of mind af-ford? They shall ob-tain this jew-el In what their hearts de-sire, When they by ad-ding fu-el Can quench the flame of fire.

lines: Can quench the flame of fire.
Till you can bid the ocean,
And rage, and swell, no more:
Come, turn your thoughts to Jesus,
When he, by faith, is present,
And all his paths are peace.
Our time in sin we wasted,
But now we stand to witness
His pow'r and grace to you;
Since we have seen his beauty,
Are joined to part no more:
And serve him with our all.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to GREENLAND by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
